notes:
Account summary:
- Healthcare org building LLM features for clinician workflow + patient communications.
- Heavy PHI constraints; they will not run production traffic through public hosted endpoints. Demo motion is Redwood Private (VPC) first, Dedicated as an interim stepping-stone only if it can be VPC-isolated.

Key stakeholders (from calls/notes):
- VP Platform Engineering (technical buyer) — wants deployment architecture + ops model.
- Security Officer / GRC (blocker owner) — focused on retention, audit, access controls.
- Product lead for clinician experience — cares about latency + output quality but will defer until security sign-off.

Current stage: Procurement
- They consider the technology direction acceptable if we can satisfy HIPAA/PHI handling and provide a credible Private deployment plan.

What we showed / what resonated:
- Demo tenant used only as UI/flow proof (explicitly said: demo environment is NOT representative of PHI handling).
- Observability: token-level cost and latency breakdown; error analysis; per-route dashboards.
- Reliability: routing/fallback behavior and how canary/rollback works when pinning model versions.
- Key message that landed: “same API + operational tooling across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, but with your security boundaries.”

Use case & technical requirements (as stated):
- Workloads:
  - Summarization of long clinician notes (often 3–8k tokens input; sometimes larger after templating).
  - Patient message triage (short chat-style + tool calling to internal systems).
  - Internal search over policies/procedures (embeddings + rerank; future phase).
- Non-functional:
  - Latency target: <2s time-to-first-token for interactive experiences; batch acceptable for back-office summarization.
  - Throughput: initial 20–40 RPS peak for portal triage; wants a plan for 10x growth.
  - Reliability: needs clear rollback/fallback story during incidents (they cited a prior vendor outage).

Security / compliance notes (blockers are mostly here):
- PHI: “No prompt/response content stored by the vendor.” They asked for a 0-day retention mode and explicit description of what remains in logs/metrics.
- Encryption:
  - In transit: TLS is table stakes.
  - At rest: expects encryption at rest for all persisted data.
  - KMS: preference for customer-managed keys in their cloud account for Private (or at minimum integration with their KMS + rotation story).
- Audit logging:
  - Wants admin audit logs (who changed routes, fallbacks, quotas, API keys, RBAC).
  - Wants export to SIEM (Splunk mentioned). They asked for format/options and whether logs can exclude payloads.
- Access controls:
  - SSO/SAML required; RBAC with least-privilege roles for platform vs developers.
  - Break-glass access expectations documented.
- Data residency:
  - US-only requirement. They asked how backups/DR are handled for Private.
- Contractual:
  - Asked whether Redwood will sign BAA for HIPAA. They also asked for SOC 2 report/letter.

Risks / watchouts:
- They keep comparing to “just self-host it” with vLLM; need to quantify operational overhead avoided (rollouts, fallback, cost controls, dashboards, regression checks).
- They are sensitive to anything that sounds like we log prompts/responses by default. We must be crisp on demo tenant vs Private defaults.

Open questions to answer in next meeting:
- Exactly what telemetry is emitted in Private, and how to configure/redact it.
- Whether audit logs include any request metadata that could be considered PHI.
- What the minimum recommended Private footprint is (clusters/regions) to meet uptime expectations.

Internal next actions:
- Markus to provide a short architecture one-pager for Redwood Private (control plane boundaries, network ingress/egress, KMS options, logging/retention controls).
- Avery to coordinate security review scheduling and keep it moving toward a documented checklist + sign-off.

Related artifacts referenced:
- Fireflies: ff-913220 (security-focused Q&A)
- Email thread: thread-4c2d77 (procurement prep / security package request)
- Support learnings to incorporate into their trial experience later: 429/throttling explanations (SUP-18411) + streaming stability mitigations (SUP-18439)

Call quotes (paraphrased):
- “We can’t have PHI going to a public endpoint, even if it’s encrypted.”
- “Audit logs are non-negotiable, but they cannot contain payloads.”
